news.title: Girls Football Festival brings friendship and opportunity to Montenegro
news.lede: Wednesday, September 23, 2026 by Aleksandar Radovic. The Girls Football Festival came to Montenegro for the first time this month, bringing together 80 girls from the region for three days of football, education and social activities. Founded in Vienna, the festival took place in the Austrian capital for six years before moving to Sarajevo in 2025. This year, it is continuing its mission of using football to promote friendship, inclusion and personal development, this time among young female players from Montenegro, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

news.title: Cerebral Palsy Football World Cup to be Hosted in Fayette
news.lede: Soccer Federation is preparing to host the 2026 International Federation of Cerebral Palsy Football Men's and Women's World Cup, marking the first time in 20 years the tournament has been held in the United States. The tournament is scheduled Oct. 12-24 and will take place at Arthur M. Soccer National Training Centre. There will be 12 men's teams and eight women's teams, from six continents, competing this year, according to officials.

news.title: Messi, Ronaldo and Bangladesh’s ASEAN Cup: A longer international break, with plenty to watch
news.lede: Club football is taking a near-three-week pause, but there is no shortage of intrigue on the international stage. For the first time, the September and October FIFA windows have been merged into a single 16-day international period, running from September 21 to October 6. Major European clubs played their last match before the break on September 20 and will return to action on October 10, leaving supporters without club football for almost three weeks. National teams, meanwhile, will pack four matches into the extended window instead of the usual two.

news.title: All Whites ready to move on from World Cup
news.lede: The All Whites will kick off the longest FIFA international window ever with a historic friendly against Palestine, but only those in Longxing Football Stadium, Chongqing, China will witness it. The first ever game between the two nations begins the new World Cup cycle and marks a period of change for both teams. Though it is expected both sides will use Thursday's match as a bit of training run and make use of the 11 available substitutes. With FIFA expanding the first international window after this year's World Cup to allow four games, rather than the traditional two, this fixture was hurriedly added to the All Whites' schedule which also includes a game against China on Monday and two matches in the Kirin Cup in Japan from 1 October.

news.title: Italy national football team players: the 34 Mancini picked after a third World Cup miss
news.lede: Roberto Mancini is back as Italy coach and has named 34 players for the Nations League, 11 of whom have never been capped. Here is the full squad, and what the caps column says about where Italy are. Italy will miss a World Cup for the third time running, and the squad Roberto Mancini has named for his first competitive matches back in the job is the first real sign of what he intends to do about it. Thirty-four players were called up for the 2026-27 Nations League games against Belgium, Turkey and France.

news.title: First World Cup win for transplant football team
news.lede: Daley Cross (left) managed the team to success, while Kevin Kyley played up front. England's transplant football team are world champions for the first time. They thrashed Spain 5-1 on Friday to take the crown in Frankfurt, Germany, taking revenge after the country knocked them out at the previous World Cup in 2024. Manager Daley Cross, from Bicester, Oxfordshire, said he could sense that his team were determined to bring the trophy home from the outset.

news.title: Italy football hopes for new dawn under returning Mancini
news.lede: Roberto Mancini, the architect of Italy’s last major triumph at Euro 2020, is back as head coach. ROME – After months of soul-searching, controversy and debate, Italy are ready to let football do the talking again as Roberto Mancini kick-starts his second spell in charge. On Sept 25, the Azzurri begin their Nations League campaign against Belgium at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome. It will be Italy’s first competitive match since a play-off defeat by Bosnia and Herzegovina in March sealed a humbling third consecutive failure to reach the World Cup Finals.
